topic: Safety precautions to be observed while working on compass, inertial navigation systems and safety precaution while working with nonmagnetic
syllabus_extract: Safety precautions to be observed while working on compass, inertial navigation systems and safety precaution while working with nonmagnetic tools on compass.
specific_objectives: 14.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain and define a position on the earth.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Demonstration of non-magnetic tool usage and compass protection; Instructor supervision required for all handling of sensitive equipment.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of the aircraft magnetic compass?
Why must non-magnetic tools be used near the compass?
What are the basic components of an Inertial Navigation System (INS)?

development.content:
Magnetic interference sources
Compass protection zones
Non-magnetic tool identification
Handling procedures for compass
INS safety protocols

Demonstration of non-magnetic tools
Simulation of compass handling
Review of EMI/EMC risks
Safety checklist verification
Instructor supervision techniques

Summary of safety rules
Q&A on specific scenarios
Reinforcement of key points
Preparation for next lesson
Final safety briefing

summary_questions: List three specific safety precautions for working near the aircraft compass.
Explain why standard steel tools are prohibited in the INS area.
Describe the immediate action required if a magnetic tool is dropped near the compass.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief report on the differences between magnetic and inertial navigation systems, referencing the block diagram to be studied in LP 10.

pft_rows.syllabus: Simple inertial navigation system block diagram.
